title: F1 Fast-Rebinding Deadline-Feasibility Replication
motivation: In the original E13 120-trial run, F1.1 and F1.2 (locked scenarios, both frozen with a 5.0s commit_deadline_s) had live delete/recreate transition durations of approximately 39-80 seconds against their 5s deadline -- structurally unable to complete within the modeled action horizon, so those 40 trials could only demonstrate functional stale-state detection, not deadline-bounded EA-TOCTOU validation. This experiment reproduces the identical same-name-UID-rebinding mechanism, but hosted on a ConfigMap instead of a Pod, isolating the identity-rebinding mechanism's timing from container-scheduling/image-pull/start latency, to test whether deadline-bounded live evidence for the F1 mechanism family is achievable.
notes: Preregistered post-hoc extension (E23), run outside the locked v8.1.1 package and outside all prior v9/E21 evidence. Uses the real, unmodified derive_critical_predicates() and commit_components() from the locked engine. The real Kubernetes-assigned metadata.uid is used as the binding evidence (not a synthetic data field), making this a faithful identity-rebinding analog of F1.1/F1.2 rather than a different mechanism.
